message: This test_forge round added strict numeric-threshold assertions to UNIT-level tests only (substitution-spec parser, jsonpatch, dataclass field counts in tests/test_cli_new_subs.py, tests/test_jsonpatch.py, tests/test_substitutions_new.py). The repo's natural end-to-end fixture is tests/fixtures/agent.py (run_recorded_agent — record -> .sb -> replay -> substitute -> re-execute, exercised by scripts/bench_replay_caching.py). None of the new strict assertions exercise that full record/replay/substitute pipeline, so the round strengthens parsing surface coverage but adds no new e2e-fixture-grounded numeric guarantees.
evidence: tests/test_cli_new_subs.py: new tests (test_sampling_kv_field_count_threshold, test_inputs_patch_op_count_matches_spec, test_message_path_roundtrip_byte_size, ...) all call parse_substitution_spec(...) and assert on the parsed dataclass — no Recorder/Replayer involvement.
tests/test_jsonpatch.py: new tests assert apply_patch length deltas on plain dicts/lists — pure helper-level.

tests/test_substitutions_new.py: new strict tests (test_system_prepend_length_bounds, test_message_patch_preserves_list_size_on_replace, ...) call sub.apply(inputs, {}) on synthetic dicts; do not run through run_recorded_agent or scripts/bench_replay_caching.py.

rule_title: Tests get equal effort to code; mutation testing must catch defects
message: The commit message labels this 'r0023 test_forge', which per rule 3b should include mutation-style validation that the new strict assertions actually catch real defects. The diff shows no mutation-testing run, no _audit/mutation_*.json artifact, and no recorded mutation-survival numbers. Several of the new asserts duplicate values in adjacent lines (e.g. asserting both `new_len == 100 + 25 + 2` and `new_len - len(base) == 27` in tests/test_substitutions_new.py::test_system_append_byte_delta_exact), which is fine for documentation but does not by itself demonstrate mutation coverage.
evidence: git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat shows no entries under _audit/mutation* or scripts/mutation*; only tests/, meta/run_obligations.md, GROUNDING.md, .kitchensink/dossier.md, _audit/findings.jsonl, _critic/findings.json and pyc files.

rule_title: One coherent thematic improvement; no bundled unrelated fixes
message: Theme of the round (strengthen test assertions with numeric thresholds) is coherent and well-scoped across the three test files. Minor hygiene note: the commit also re-stages numerous compiled stepback/__pycache__/*.pyc and tests/__pycache__/*.pyc files, which are tracked in this repo but bloat the diff and are unrelated to the thematic change. Pre-existing tracking of .pyc is not this commit's fault, but the round could have refrained from re-committing them.
evidence: git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat: 11 of 24 changed paths are .pyc files under stepback/__pycache__/ or tests/__pycache__/.
.gitignore does not list __pycache__/ or *.pyc — pre-existing repo policy tracks them.
